column1: # Passive and drive components required BEYOND the modules in control-system-bom.csv. Derived from the h743-pin-allocation.csv channel list. Two rows are marked SAFETY-CRITICAL: the SSR gate pull-downs and the valve relay pull resistors. Both exist to keep a load DE-ENERGISED when the MCU is in reset, booting, or hung with its GPIOs high-impedance - the state OBL-ELECTRICAL-THERMAL-SAFETY-001.C2 names. Neither is optional and neither is on any purchased module.

column5: The EARU SSR-40DA needs 7.5-12mA at 3-32VDC; a 3V3 GPIO sourcing 12mA sags below the SSR's 3V minimum. The ULN2003A sinks each SSR's control input from the 5V rail instead
column7: Two of its seven channels are used (IN1/IN2 from PB0/PB1). About 24mA total for both: the SSR control current (2 x up to 12mA) drawn from the 5V rail through the ULN2003A, not a GPIO current; the 5V budget in module-interconnect.csv carries 29mA for it (24mA SSR control current (the 29mA in the 5V budget is not reconciled with it)). Darlington drop about 1V so the SSR sees about 4V - measure it. Replaces the earlier 2N7002/BSS138 design

column2: Pull-DOWN to GND on each ULN2003A input (IN1, IN2)
column5: Holds the SSR drive off while the MCU is in reset, booting, or has crashed with GPIOs high-impedance. The chip should also default off through its own input resistors, but that is a datasheet claim not yet confirmed on this breakout
column7: Without this a floating input could energise a heater with no firmware running - precisely the case OBL-ELECTRICAL-THERMAL-SAFETY-001.C2 forbids. Fit it AT THE BREAKOUT BOARD, across each used IN pin and the board's GND pin (short leads under the board; confirm that GND pin is the chip's pin 8 by meter), not on the perfboard: at the module end it holds the input off whether the GPIO is floating or the cable has come off. Once the breakout's input behaviour is measured floating this may become belt-and-braces, but it is cheap and stays

column5: The SSR-xxDA input has its own current-limiting front end: a 3-32VDC input spec with a 7.5-12mA drive current is only possible with a built-in limiter, since a bare LED with a fixed series resistor would draw several times more at 32V than at 3V
column7: Owner's judgement, consistent with the spec's own figures. First bench check: with the SSR wired through the ULN2003A at about 4V, measure the control current - it should sit near 7.5-12mA

column5: Forms the divider with each NTC; the board has no analog conditioning. 5 channels: 2 PT1000 (the outlet water spike probe and the temporary puck-inlet probe) and 3 NTCs (coffee block, steam block, wand). The 4.7k also suits the PT1000: about 0.54mA, 0.4mW self-heating, about 1.6mV/C
column7: Value settled at 4.7k. SPECIFY BY TCR, NOT INITIAL TOLERANCE: three-point Steinhart-Hart calibration solves for the gain term, so initial tolerance is absorbed - what calibration cannot absorb is drift. This supersedes the earlier 1% / 0.1% advice. Wire the divider from VREF+/VDDA so the measurement is RATIOMETRIC and supply variation cancels - free, and it removes reference error from the budget entirely

column5: Charge reservoir for the ADC sampling capacitor, and a low-pass against switching noise
column7: REQ-ELECTRICAL-INSTALL-001.C8 requires sensing to hold accuracy WHILE the kW loads switch. With ~1k source impedance this rolls off around 1.6kHz - far above a thermal signal sampled at 100Hz

column5: I2C is open-drain and needs external pull-ups; the H743's internal ~40k is far too weak
column7: VERIFY whether the XDB401 breakout already fits pull-ups - if both ends do, the parallel value may be too low. Drop to 2.2k only if the run is long or edges look slow
